2004: "The Local was founded in Stockholm in 2004 by Paul Rapacioli, formerly a director of reed.co.uk and managing editor James Savage, formerly a radio journalist and PR consultant."
2004: "Rapacioli was managing director from 2004-2018."
2004: "The original Swedish edition began in early 2004 as a weekly email newsletter which Paul Rapacioli started sending to other students in his "Swedish for Immigrants" class."
2004: "The first news site was launched in Sweden in August 2004."
2008: "The German edition was launched in 2008 and Swiss edition in 2011."
2010: "In 2010, following the death of its creator, The Local acquired Englishforum.ch, a chat forum for English-speaking expatriates in Switzerland."
2013: "In 2013 the company opened offices in France, Spain and Italy."
2015: "By January 2015 the company claimed to have over 4.5 million readers per month."
2018: "James Savage succeeded Paul Rapacioli as managing director in 2018."

2024: "In February 2024, both the English Forum for Switzerland and the German Toytown forum were closed, with moderators receiving notice that the company had determined that server costs were too high."
2009: "In 2009, The Local acquired the website Toytown Germany from its founder, James Pearn, who was subsequently hired by The Local as their Chief technology officer."
2010: "In January 2010 The Local acquired the thelocal.com domain name from First Quench Retailing, a UK alcohol retailer which went into administration at the end of 2009."
